title: Dimension of a standard graded algebra is attained at the vertex
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $S=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}S_j$ be a standard graded $k$-algebra [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], with $S_0=k$ and finitely many degree-one algebra generators. The irrelevant ideal $\mathfrak m=S_+=\bigoplus_{j>0}S_j$ is maximal, and localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] at this ideal preserves Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]: $$\dim S_{\mathfrak m}=\dim S.$$ No reducedness, domain or positive-dimension hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00P6, lemma-dimension-graded, proof, first equality paragraph: dim(S)=dim_x Spec(S)=dim(S_m). This part precedes, and does not use, the Hilbert-function comparison; it uses homogeneous minimal primes (Tag 00JU, lemma-graded-ring-minimal-prime) and dimension at a point (Tag 00OT, lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field).

proof.text: The degree-zero projection $\epsilon:S\to S_0=k$ is a ring homomorphism: in a nonnegative grading, the degree-zero part of a product is the product of the degree-zero parts. It is surjective on constants and has kernel $\mathfrak m=S_+$. Thus $S/\mathfrak m=k$ is a field, so $\mathfrak m$ is maximal (and prime). The finite list of degree-one generators also makes $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 00P6, lemma-dimension-graded, assertion (1) and proof, first sentence.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q$ be any minimal prime of $S$ (a prime containing no strictly smaller prime). By [lem-sfb-prime-homogeneous-core], its homogeneous core $\mathfrak q^*$ is a homogeneous prime contained in $\mathfrak q$; minimality gives $\mathfrak q^*=\mathfrak q$. For $a\in\mathfrak q$, its degree-zero component $a_0$ therefore lies in $\mathfrak q\cap k$. A nonzero element of $k$ is a unit in $S$, so properness forces $a_0=0$. Hence $a\in S_+$, proving that every minimal prime is contained in $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 00JU, lemma-graded-ring-minimal-prime, proof via Tag 00JT, lemma-smear-out; Tag 00P6, assertion (2).

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and let $x$ correspond to $\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-components] to the finite type $k$-algebra $S$ at $x$. It gives a non-negative integer $n=\dim_xX$, equal to the attained maximum of $\dim(S/\mathfrak q)$ for minimal primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$. By step 2 these are all minimal primes of $S$. The same cited statement gives $\dim_xX=\min_{\mathfrak n\supseteq\mathfrak m}\dim S_{\mathfrak n}$ over maximal ideals $\mathfrak n$. Since $\mathfrak m$ is maximal, this family has the single member $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m$, so $\dim S_{\mathfrak m}=n$.

source.place: Tag 00P6, proof, first equality paragraph, using Tag 00OT, lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, equality of (1), (2), (3).

proof.text: For any point $y\in X$, another application of [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-components] expresses $\dim_yX$ as the maximum of $\dim(S/\mathfrak q)$ over minimal primes contained in the prime of $y$. This is a subfamily of the family in step 3, so $\dim_yX\le n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions], $\dim X=\sup_y\dim_yX\le n$; the point $x$ gives the reverse inequality. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] identifies $\dim X$ with $\dim S$. Therefore $\dim S= n=\dim S_{\mathfrak m}$.
